tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your morning brief for Monday, September 21st.

Let's start with the macro picture. Futures are in the green this morning — S&P up about 65 basis points, Nasdaq up 110 basis points, Russell up 47 basis points. Asia closed broadly higher overnight, led by Korea up 1.65% and the Hang Seng up 1.18%. Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points with data center infrastructure names outperforming. Treasuries have a bid with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve. Brent crude is sliding about 170 basis points to around $102 a barrel. Bitcoin is surging 350 basis points to around $83,900.

Here is the thing — this rally is confusing. Nearly every piece of news from the weekend was net negative. The Houthis launched a major missile and drone attack on Saudi Arabia. Ukraine hit Russia with its largest drone strike of the war. Multiple troubling AI headlines dropped after Friday's close. So why are futures up? One word: diplomacy. The UN General Assembly kicks off this week in New York. Trump reportedly called off Houthi air strikes at the last minute Sunday night and said he's open to meeting Iran's president, who is expected to attend. Markets are betting that even a tiny improvement in Middle East tensions could send oil sharply lower — and if oil falls sustainably, it unlocks a cascade of bullish effects: lower yields, less hawkish monetary policy, margin relief, and better consumer confidence.

Now the key risks. Fed officials are getting louder on inflation. Kansas City Fed President Schmid and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari both warned this weekend that inflation is spreading well beyond energy. The market is pricing in about 33 basis points of additional hikes this year, with roughly even odds of a move at the October 28th meeting. Treasury is also planning to issue over one trillion dollars in T-bills over the next twelve months, leaning heavily on short-term financing.

On the company side, Oracle is in focus after a negative report highlighting that efforts to offload debt tied to its massive New Mexico data center — called Project Jupiter — have hit a wall. This comes alongside a broader story about Big Tech off-balance sheet AI liabilities rising roughly $300 billion in just the past year. OpenAI is projecting negative free cash flow of around $280 billion through 2030. Anthropic's IPO is delayed. These are not small numbers and the AI infrastructure trade deserves scrutiny here.

Novo Nordisk fell in European trading after disappointing investors at its analyst day by failing to provide specific financial targets. Disney is a relative bright spot — its parks business is outperforming peers by using price promotions and package deals to sustain traffic while competitors see headwinds. Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery remain in a complicated regulatory situation with California's attorney general, with a settlement potentially requiring CNN editorial independence protections and cable channel divestitures.

Looking ahead this week: the big macro events are the flash September PMIs on Wednesday morning and the Trump-Xi summit on Thursday, which could bring modest tariff relief on around $30 billion worth of goods. Mark Zuckerberg delivers the keynote at Meta's Connect conference Wednesday night at 7pm Eastern.

The directional read: cautiously mixed with a short-term bullish tilt, but it is entirely dependent on geopolitical headlines. The UN General Assembly is the catalyst to watch. If diplomacy delivers even a whisper of progress on Iran, this market could move hard. If tensions escalate further, the rally fades fast. Trade accordingly.
